source.snippet: Given that my Next.js + Strapi website receives about 286,000 page views per year and currently scores ~70–100 on desktop and ~60–90 on mobile in PageSpeed Insights (with GTM as the main bottleneck), how can I determine whether these performance scores are already sufficient for real users and business impact, or whether migrating to server-side GTM would meaningfully improve outcomes?

problem_statement: Business website operators with meaningful traffic cannot determine whether investing in server-side tag management migration is worth the cost and complexity, leaving them stuck with client-side GTM that degrades Core Web Vitals and potentially SEO rankings.
target_segment: Marketing and web ops teams at SMBs and agencies running Next.js or similar sites with 100k+ annual page views
notes: Poster has a real commercial site (286k page views/year), is already considering a paid infrastructure upgrade (server-side GTM has hosting costs), and is trying to make an ROI decision. Buyer context is clear. Opportunity: a ROI calculator or audit service for GTM migration decisions; or a managed server-side GTM migration service. Single post keeps signal low, but the question pattern is common across webmaster/SEO communities.
